messages:
kai: FYI during the quarterly access review I spotted ~24 admin-style grants tied to our prod KMS key in the last 30d. Not expected.
mike: ugh. are these user approvals or service-account grants?
sara: going to pull logs now, give me 2.
audit-bot: evidence-ingest: 24 KMS GRANT events flagged (rule: unexpected-admin-grant). ticket INC-5567 created.
eva: @kai can you paste the key-id / region? I want to run a quick diff vs last snapshot.
kai: key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/us-west1/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/primary (aws alias: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-1234)
sara: quick grep shows most grants are from an internal tool 'key-manager' svcacct and a handful from users alice/bob/charles.
mike: if 'key-manager' started auto-approving, that would explain the surge. @eva can you check the deploy history for that tool?
eva: checking... found a canary deploy of key-manager on 2026-03-18 with a config change: enable-auto-approve: true
kai: ok let's treat this like a vuln/privilege incident. Triage plan: 1) freeze auto-approve 2) revoke unexpected grants 3) rotate key or create new key + re-encrypt 4) run least-priv audit and recertify owners.
sara: I can run revoke script for the user grants now: ```aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-1234 --query Grants[]``` then filter by GranteePrincipal and `aws kms revoke-grant --grant-id <id>`
mike: please only revoke user grants first, leave svcacct grants until we confirm impact. Document before/after snapshot in INC-5567.
eva: I've reverted the canary flag to enable-auto-approve: false and rolled out a block to prod-key-manager (deploy-bot blocked 1 job). deploy-bot: deployment rollback initiated by eva at 2026-03-19T15:12Z :arrow_down:
kai: good. @sara when revoking, include command outputs in the ticket and run `--dry-run` style where available.
sara: revoking user grants now, adding notes to INC-5567. one user grant failed to revoke (403). suspect entitlement binding elsewhere.
mike: if revoke fails, capture IAM policy, svc bindings, and open a follow-up to remove entitlement at the source. tag infra-oncall.
kai: also need KMS audit logs to be exported to long-term storage and set an alert rule: failed revokes, new grants > 5/day. @eva can you add alert runbook link?
eva: added alert: Audit > KMS unexpected grants, notify #eng-security + paged on SEV2. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-privilege-surge
audit-bot: log-export: incremental export to gs://redwood-audit/kms/2026-03-19 done.
sara: user grants revoked: alice, bob. charles revoke failed (403) — filing follow-up with infra ACL owner. snapshot attached to INC-5567.
mike: schedule a short postmortem tomorrow 10:00. focus items: root cause, improved gating for auto-approve, 7-day recert of all admin grants, KMS grant retention policy.
kai: agree. also add a policy: any auto-approve flag must require explicit 2-person approval and a feature-flagged rollout blocked for >3 grants/day
eva: I'll add a RBAC patch proposal: ```{
  "bindings": [
    {"role":"roles/kms.admin","members":["serviceAccount:key-manager@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"], "condition": "request.time < '2026-03-25T00:00:00Z'"}
  ]
}```
mike: thanks. @audit-bot can you produce a short CSV of grants by principal + timestamp and attach to INC-5567?
audit-bot: attached /artifacts/inc-5567/kms_grants_20260319.csv
kai: thanks everyone. immediate: monitor for any new grants for 24h, don't rotate key unless we confirm service impact. we'll cover rotation as contingency in the postmortem
eva: noted. pinging infra-oncall separately for the charles revoke and potential IAM cleanup.
mike: copy. closing loop here once INC-5567 has the revoke outputs and the RBAC patch PR is open.
kai: closing for now — will update thread with postmortem invite and schedule. :thumbsup:
